result.rationale: The diff shows findMembers calling Discourse.ajax('/groups/' + this.get('name') + '/members.json') while the admin group form binds the editable name via {{text-field name="name" value=name ...}}. Since addMembers, removeMember, next, and previous all call findMembers using the (possibly unsaved, edited) name while mutations (PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:id) target the id, an unsaved rename causes member reads to hit a different (or nonexistent) group. The mechanism is verifiable directly from the diff, though severity depends on unsaved-name workflow.

judged_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:25 — Using `Discourse.ajax('/groups/' + this.get('name') + '/members.json', {` couples membership identity to the draft name bound by `{{text-field name="name" value=name placeholderKey="admin.groups.name_placeholder"}}`, so an administrator editing group A's name to existing group B and then paging or adding a member replaces A's displayed membership/count with B's even though writes still target A through `this.get('id')`; the strongest rebuttal is that names are the public endpoint's established identifier, but independent membership actions now run before Save, so separating draft attributes from persisted identity or using an ID-based read is necessary and eliminates draft-name lookup dependencies from both mutation refreshes and page navigation.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug in the diff. Looking at the code: findMembers() uses `this.get('name')` to fetch members (line 25), while addMembers() and removeMember() use `this.get('id')` for mutations. The template shows the name field is editable via `{{text-field name="name" value=name}}`. If an admin edits the group name to match another existing group's name before saving, then calls findMembers() (via pagination or after addMembers/removeMember which both call findMembers()), it will fetch members from the group matching the draft name, not the actual group being edited. This creates a state inconsistency where the displayed members don't match the group being modified. The diff clearly shows this pattern: mutations use ID, reads use name, and name is editable before save.
